passages.name: sexedClassmateConvo
passages.source_raw: <><>@@.you;$name: So, do you think it's possible to learn everything about sexual health from a textbook?@@ $classmateName: If I learned everything from a textbook, I'd be *way* too paranoid to leave the house. @@.you;$name: I'm pretty sure some textbooks are more confusing than helpful anyway.@@<>@@.you;$name: Okay, but seriously, do you think we should be teaching younger kids about consent in school?@@ $classmateName: I think it's a must. You wouldn't give someone your phone without asking, right? @@.you;$name: Exactly! Consent is *the* key.@@<>@@.you;$name: If someone says "no," is it always clear? Like, should we just automatically take it as a hard stop?@@ $classmateName: Of course. "No" means "no." Period. Anything less than that is *way* too blurry. @@.you;$name: I think people forget how powerful a simple word can be.@@<>@@.you;$name: You know, I read that STDs can be spread even if you don't have symptoms. That's wild.@@ $classmateName: Yep, it's like an invisible game of tag, but no one's having fun. @@.you;$name: So, basically, regular checkups should be a *thing* for everyone.@@<>@@.you;$name: How do you even begin talking to someone about birth control? That conversation feels impossible.@@ $classmateName: It's not as bad as you think. Just be open. Like, “Hey, let's talk about our options so we're both on the same page!” @@.you;$name: I guess that sounds a lot better than, “So... birth control, huh?”@@<>@@.you;$name: Can we just talk about how weird the first sex ed class is? Like, no one knows what to say.@@ $classmateName: It's the only time in school where everyone suddenly becomes an expert *and* a rookie at the same time. @@.you;$name: Honestly, half the time, I don't know whether to laugh or be embarrassed.@@<>@@.you;$name: So, like, if we're all told that sex should be enjoyable, does that apply to everyone? Even for people who aren't in relationships?@@ $classmateName: Yeah! Enjoyment is for everyone, no matter the situation. It's about mutual respect, not just "couple stuff." @@.you;$name: I like how simple that is! Enjoyment is a basic human right.@@<>@@.you;$name: You ever wonder if people even realize how important boundaries are? It's kind of basic, but also super complex.@@ $classmateName: Boundaries are everything. Without them, everything gets messy. Respect goes both ways. @@.you;$name: You're right. It's like building a friendship first before anything else.@@<>@@.you;$name: If someone's not into something, does that mean they *should* say something?@@ $classmateName: Yeah, it's about speaking up and respecting others' limits. It's *always* okay to say no. @@.you;$name: Definitely better than pretending it's okay when it's not.@@<>@@.you;$name: Why do you think people are so awkward talking about sex? Like, what's the big deal?@@ $classmateName: I think it's just society's weird way of making something totally normal feel taboo. @@.you;$name: It's just another part of life, but somehow, we've made it feel so off-limits.@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you ever feel like people make too big of a deal out of waiting until you're older to have sex?@@ $classmateName: Honestly, it depends on the person. It's about maturity and when you're ready-not an age. @@.you;$name: That makes sense. People should *feel* ready, not just be “old enough.”@@<>@@.you;$name: Wait, are we really supposed to just *know* how to talk about contraception? Where's the manual for this?@@ $classmateName: If there's no manual, maybe we should write one! We're *definitely* overdue for better education. @@.you;$name: I'd totally sign up to make the “Sex Ed: For Dummies” edition.@@<>@@.you;$name: What if someone is scared to talk about their sexual health with a doctor?@@ $classmateName: Doctors are there to help, not judge. They see it all the time, no big deal. @@.you;$name: Right! It's like they're professionals. We're all human after all.@@<>@@.you;$name: I wonder how people even figure out what's healthy for them when it comes to sex. Does it just “click”?@@ $classmateName: It's a process. You learn your limits, communicate, and get better at it. @@.you;$name: It's like any relationship, really. Understanding is key!@@<>@@.you;$name: Why do people talk so much about the “perfect first time” when really, it's about comfort?@@ $classmateName: Society loves to romanticize things. But at the end of the day, comfort is everything. @@.you;$name: Exactly! You're not supposed to feel pressured to be perfect.@@<>@@.you;$name: Why is there so much emphasis on being “experienced”? Does that really matter?@@ $classmateName: Nah, experience is personal. It's all about respect and feeling comfortable in the situation. @@.you;$name: Right! Everyone's at their own pace. Who's keeping score anyway?@@<>@@.you;$name: So if someone says they're not ready, but they like you, what should you do?@@ $classmateName: You respect that! You build trust first and wait until both people are comfortable. @@.you;$name: That's the right call. Trust comes before everything.@@<>@@.you;$name: What do you think about the “everyone's doing it” mentality? Does that make a difference?@@ $classmateName: It only matters if you're ready, not what others are doing. @@.you;$name: So true! It's not a race; it's about personal choice.@@<>@@.you;$name: What's the best way to start talking to your partner about safer sex?@@ $classmateName: Just be straightforward. It's better to talk than to *not* talk. Safety first! @@.you;$name: Agreed! A healthy relationship starts with healthy communication.@@<>@@.you;$name: I think people should be more open about talking about their feelings and their sexual health. It shouldn't be a “taboo.”@@ $classmateName: 100%! The more we talk about it, the less awkward it gets for everyone. @@.you;$name: Exactly! Let's make these conversations normal, not weird.@@<>

passages.name: biologyClassmateConvo
passages.source_raw: <><>@@.you;$name: Do you ever think about how everything in nature is connected? Like, it's all one big web.@@ $classmateName: Absolutely. Like, without bees, we wouldn't have most of our food! @@.you;$name: And yet, people are still afraid of them! I don't get it.@@<>@@.you;$name: I just realized, our entire existence is basically one big ecosystem.@@ $classmateName: We're just tiny pieces of the puzzle. So wild! @@.you;$name: And yet we think we're the most important part.@@<>@@.you;$name: If I were an animal, I think I'd be a sloth. No rush, just vibing all day.@@ $classmateName: I can see that. You'd be hanging out, taking naps, living the dream. @@.you;$name: Exactly! Sloth life for me.@@<>@@.you;$name: What do you think would happen if we swapped places with dolphins for a day?@@ $classmateName: I bet it'd be *way* more fun. Dolphins are literally the party animals of the ocean! @@.you;$name: Right? I'd be swimming through the ocean, having the time of my life.@@<>@@.you;$name: So, plants talk to each other through their roots? That's pretty insane.@@ $classmateName: Yeah, it's like plant gossip. “Did you hear about that new compost over there?” @@.you;$name: Imagine how much drama is happening in the dirt.@@<>@@.you;$name: I think the mitochondria should be the most famous part of biology. It's literally the powerhouse!@@ $classmateName: Yeah, without mitochondria, we'd have no energy. The unsung heroes of our cells. @@.you;$name: They should get their own award. They deserve it.@@<>@@.you;$name: How crazy is it that humans have more bacterial cells than human cells in their bodies?@@ $classmateName: That's wild! We're basically a walking ecosystem for bacteria. @@.you;$name: So, are we the hosts or the guests here?@@<>@@.you;$name: I just learned that the blue whale's heart is the size of a car!@@ $classmateName: That's insane! A heart that big must be a serious workout. @@.you;$name: I bet it's got to be the most *extra* heart in the animal kingdom.@@<>@@.you;$name: Imagine if our brains were like computers, just constantly processing everything.@@ $classmateName: That would be *way* too much for me. I already get overwhelmed just trying to finish my homework. @@.you;$name: Yeah, but imagine how fast you'd be at multitasking!@@<>@@.you;$name: I think if I were a plant, I'd be a cactus. Surviving in tough conditions with little effort.@@ $classmateName: You'd definitely be the cactus type. Low maintenance but strong! @@.you;$name: Exactly, just give me some sunlight and I'm good.@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you ever think about how some animals can regenerate body parts? Like, starfish can grow a whole new arm!@@ $classmateName: I'm just waiting for science to make that happen for humans. I'd love a new arm if I ever lose one. @@.you;$name: Right? Imagine if we could regrow entire limbs like some animals.@@<>@@.you;$name: If we could communicate with animals, do you think we'd learn a lot about their lives?@@ $classmateName: I think we'd be shocked by how much drama is going on in the animal kingdom. @@.you;$name: Like, “Hey, I saw you steal that fish, don't act innocent!”@@<>@@.you;$name: Sometimes I think about how every living thing on Earth is made of the same basic elements. It's kind of poetic.@@ $classmateName: We're all connected in some weird, chemical way. Like one big cosmic family. @@.you;$name: It's like we're all part of the same story.@@<>@@.you;$name: The idea that we evolved from simple cells is so mind-blowing to me.@@ $classmateName: It's crazy! That's like going from building blocks to entire cities. @@.you;$name: Yeah, how does that even happen? It's like the ultimate underdog story.@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you think we could ever create life artificially, like in Frankenstein?@@ $classmateName: If we do, I'm hoping it's less *monster* and more *really cool robot*. @@.you;$name: Honestly, I'd take a robot friend over a monster any day.@@<>@@.you;$name: Isn't it wild that some animals can sleep for months? Like, how does that even work?@@ $classmateName: That's like me during finals week. Just hibernate until it's over. @@.you;$name: Same, honestly. Sleep is an art form.@@<>@@.you;$name: You ever wonder how fish can breathe underwater? It's like they have superpowers.@@ $classmateName: It's like they have a built-in filter. I wish I had that for my water bottle. @@.you;$name: Right? I need a fish's secret life hack.@@<>@@.you;$name: What do you think about the idea that we're all just a bunch of chemicals reacting to stimuli?@@ $classmateName: It sounds kind of like a science fiction plot, but honestly, it makes sense. @@.you;$name: So, we're all just complex biochemical machines. Cool.@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you think plants actually "feel" things when we talk to them? Like, do they have emotions?@@ $classmateName: I wouldn't be surprised. They react to their environment, so who knows? @@.you;$name: I'm definitely going to try talking to my plants more often. Maybe I'll get better at keeping them alive.@@<>@@.you;$name: If we could ever discover life on another planet, what do you think it would be like?@@ $classmateName: Probably like the stuff we see in sci-fi, but less dangerous. I'm hoping for some friendly aliens. @@.you;$name: I'd love to find out we're just one part of an intergalactic community.@@<>

passages.name: anatomyClassmateConvo
passages.source_raw: <><>@@.you;$name: I can't believe we have muscles in places we never think about. Like, there's a muscle just for moving your ears!@@ $classmateName: Honestly, the human body is so extra. We have muscles for everything! @@.you;$name: Right? I wonder if I can get my ears to move on command.@@<>@@.you;$name: You ever think about how our body's basically a giant electrical system? We have nerves like wires running everywhere.@@ $classmateName: I'm just waiting for someone to invent a USB port in my arm for easy charging. @@.you;$name: I mean, if we're wired like that, might as well upgrade us, right?@@<>@@.you;$name: Imagine if our bones could talk. What would they say after carrying all this weight around all the time?@@ $classmateName: They'd probably be like, “Yo, take a break. I need some calcium.” @@.you;$name: Probably complaining about the lack of vitamin D, too.@@<>@@.you;$name: Did you know your body has more bacteria cells than human cells? It's like we're walking ecosystems.@@ $classmateName: I feel like I'm hosting a party inside my body. So many guests! @@.you;$name: Yeah, but they don't clean up after themselves. I wish they'd take out the trash once in a while.@@<>@@.you;$name: I can't believe our lungs are like balloons. They just inflate and deflate all day.@@ $classmateName: So if we're inflatable, does that mean we're like human beach balls? @@.you;$name: I hope we don't get kicked around like one.@@<>@@.you;$name: I was thinking, the human body is basically like a car. It has parts that need to be maintained, like oil for our joints.@@ $classmateName: That's why I try to stretch every day-gotta keep the engine running smoothly. @@.you;$name: Just need some premium fuel...aka coffee.@@<>@@.you;$name: You know, the heart's pretty dramatic. It literally works *non-stop* for your whole life.@@ $classmateName: It's like the MVP of your body, never asking for a break. @@.you;$name: It's like a bodyguard that never stops working, even when you're sleeping.@@<>@@.you;$name: Have you ever thought about how our skin's the body's largest organ? It's like, we wear an entire outfit every day!@@ $classmateName: Yeah, except it's the outfit that you can never take off! Not even for laundry day. @@.you;$name: It's like a permanent costume. We should get to pick a new one every year.@@<>@@.you;$name: I read that the average person blinks 15-20 times per minute. That's a lot of blinks!@@ $classmateName: So, like, our eyes are constantly on a blink-break cycle. No wonder I get tired. @@.you;$name: Right? Blink too much and you'll end up with dry eyes. Blink too little, and you're a weirdo.@@<>@@.you;$name: I love that our stomachs can hold like 1-2 liters of food. It's like we're walking food storage containers.@@ $classmateName: Imagine if we could actually store stuff like that. I'd fill mine with snacks! @@.you;$name: Same. My stomach would be like a snack warehouse.@@<>@@.you;$name: The fact that we can move all our fingers independently is so cool. Think of how much work that takes!@@ $classmateName: I've got pretty good finger control. It's like my fingers have their own little party going on. @@.you;$name: Same, but sometimes I feel like my pinky just wants to do its own thing.@@<>@@.you;$name: I wonder if we have a muscle in our body that controls our procrastination. Because mine is strong.@@ $classmateName: Yeah, I think that muscle is called “the snooze button.” @@.you;$name: My procrastination muscle could probably bench press a house.@@<>@@.you;$name: The fact that we have a muscle called the "levator ani" is hilarious. It's responsible for lifting certain parts of your body.@@ $classmateName: The name makes it sound like it should be in a superhero movie! @@.you;$name: Exactly! Levator Ani, Defender of the Lower Body.@@<>@@.you;$name: Have you ever wondered what your body would do if you suddenly decided to start sprinting right now?@@ $classmateName: My body would probably be like, “Wait, are you sure about this?” @@.you;$name: Yeah, and then my legs would just give up and send me into a full tumble.@@<>@@.you;$name: I think it's amazing that our body can heal itself after injury. Like, our skin just knows how to get better.@@ $classmateName: Yeah, it's like a built-in repair system. I wish my phone had that. @@.you;$name: Seriously! I'd love a self-repairing phone. I'd never worry about dropping it again.@@<>@@.you;$name: The fact that we have a whole system just for our senses is wild. Like, sight, hearing, taste...all separate departments.@@ $classmateName: It's like a big sensory office, and they all report back to the brain every day. @@.you;$name: Imagine if they had office meetings. “Okay, hearing, what did you pick up today?”@@<>@@.you;$name: Our bones are super strong, yet they're constantly being broken down and rebuilt. It's like construction workers at all times!@@ $classmateName: Yeah, our bones are like little mini construction projects. @@.you;$name: I just hope they don't mess up and give me a crooked arm!@@<>@@.you;$name: The human body is pretty amazing, but let's be real, sometimes it just breaks down. Why do we need to hiccup?@@ $classmateName: Maybe it's like our body's way of saying “Hey, I'm still here!” @@.you;$name: Yeah, but why the weird noise? It's like an emergency siren going off.@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you think our body's immune system gets tired of fighting off germs all the time?@@ $classmateName: I think it's probably like, “Can we get a vacation already?” @@.you;$name: Honestly, it deserves a spa day.@@<>@@.you;$name: The fact that we have more than 600 muscles is wild. No wonder I'm always sore!@@ $classmateName: I feel like I'm sore just from existing at this point. @@.you;$name: Same, I think my muscles need a break!@@<>

passages.name: mathClassmateConvo
passages.source_raw: <><>@@.you;$name: I can't believe we're still solving for x. What does x even want from us?@@ $classmateName: X is just out here living its best life, never telling us what it needs. @@.you;$name: I feel like it's been playing hard-to-get for way too long.@@<>@@.you;$name: Math problems make me feel like I'm trying to solve a mystery, but the answers are always so far out of reach.@@ $classmateName: It's like being in a crime scene, and all we find are equations instead of clues! @@.you;$name: Right? I'm just waiting for the answer to turn up like a suspect.@@<>@@.you;$name: Why does math have to be so dramatic? It's always like “Solve for x,” but it never tells you why x is missing in the first place.@@ $classmateName: X is just a rebel, always disappearing and leaving us to clean up the mess. @@.you;$name: If x were a person, it'd be the friend who never answers their texts.@@<>@@.you;$name: I'm convinced that math teachers invented word problems just to test how good we are at reading.@@ $classmateName: Word problems are basically a game of “Can you even comprehend what I'm saying?” @@.you;$name: Exactly! I spend more time trying to decode the question than actually solving it.@@<>@@.you;$name: The way math makes us memorize formulas feels like they're trying to make us into walking calculators.@@ $classmateName: I'm just waiting for someone to hand me a memory upgrade already. @@.you;$name: Same, I need some kind of shortcut to the brain's RAM.@@<>@@.you;$name: Can we talk about how pi is literally the most mysterious number in the world? It's never-ending, like a cosmic mystery.@@ $classmateName: Pi is the universe's way of saying “You'll never know everything.” @@.you;$name: Pi is like that one friend who always has more stories to tell but never finishes any of them.@@<>@@.you;$name: If math was a reality show, I feel like algebra would be the main villain. It's just always making things hard for us.@@ $classmateName: Algebra would be the one who keeps changing the rules mid-game. @@.you;$name: Exactly! It's always throwing in new variables when you least expect it.@@<>@@.you;$name: You ever look at a complicated equation and wonder if the universe is just testing us for fun?@@ $classmateName: Definitely. The universe is probably sitting back, laughing at us like, “They'll never figure it out.” @@.you;$name: It's like math is the ultimate prank.@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like every time I finish a math problem, there's always another one waiting to ruin my life.@@ $classmateName: It's like math problems are never-ending side quests. Just when you think you're done, another one pops up. @@.you;$name: Exactly! It's like playing a video game with infinite levels.@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you think math teachers get excited when we ask for help, or are they just used to our panic?@@ $classmateName: I think they're just happy to have someone who still cares at all! @@.you;$name: Fair. I would be too if I had to explain this stuff all day.@@<>@@.you;$name: You know, I always wondered what would happen if I just multiplied everything by zero. Would the world just collapse?@@ $classmateName: Honestly, if you multiplied everything by zero, we'd probably end up in an alternate universe where math doesn't exist. @@.you;$name: That's terrifying and also kind of fascinating.@@<>@@.you;$name: Sometimes I wish math could just make sense the first time. But no, it's always a game of trial and error.@@ $classmateName: Math is like a puzzle, except you don't get the box with the picture on it. @@.you;$name: It's like solving a mystery, but no one tells you if you're on the right track.@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like math would be way cooler if we had superheroes for numbers. Like, Captain Fraction!@@ $classmateName: Ooh, I'd love to see “The Incredible Integer” take on the villain, Chaos Variable. @@.you;$name: And then, of course, there's the unbeatable Pi Man who just never ends.@@<>@@.you;$name: What if math was actually just a secret code for the universe, and we're all decoding it without knowing?@@ $classmateName: You mean like a hidden language of the cosmos? I'm into it. @@.you;$name: Yeah, like, what if all our equations are actually messages from aliens?@@<>@@.you;$name: Honestly, sometimes I think that math problems are just the universe's way of reminding us how small we are.@@ $classmateName: Math is a constant reminder that we'll never truly understand everything. @@.you;$name: It's like the universe is saying, “Yeah, you're smart, but you still can't figure out this simple addition.”@@<>@@.you;$name: If I could get paid for every time I stared at a math problem and wondered what went wrong, I'd be rich.@@ $classmateName: You'd be living in a mansion by now. @@.you;$name: I'd probably use all that money to pay for math tutoring.@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like math is just one big game of “Guess what the teacher's thinking.”@@ $classmateName: It's like we're trying to figure out the secret code that they've never actually explained to us. @@.you;$name: Yeah, they give us the answer, but never the key to unlock it.@@<>@@.you;$name: You ever feel like you're in a relationship with math, but it's super toxic? Like, you try so hard, and it keeps rejecting you.@@ $classmateName: It's like we keep giving it all we have, and it's just “No, sorry, try again.” @@.you;$name: Honestly, math could at least text us back once in a while.@@<>@@.you;$name: If math was a language, I feel like I'd be that person who speaks it *just enough* to get by, but never fluently.@@ $classmateName: Yeah, I'm like the tourist who's memorized a few key phrases, but still looks confused at every turn. @@.you;$name: Same, I just know enough to order the math equivalent of coffee.@@<>@@.you;$name: I think math is secretly a test of patience. It just wants to see how long you'll stare at it before you give up.@@ $classmateName: Honestly, I've stared at an equation for so long, I think it's judging me now. @@.you;$name: If math could talk, it'd probably say, “You still haven't solved me? Try harder.”@@<>

passages.name: computerClassmateConvo
passages.source_raw: <><>@@.you;$name: Do you ever feel like computers are secretly judging us for typing too slow?@@ $classmateName: Yeah, like they're just sitting there, silently mocking our every typo. @@.you;$name: I swear my computer has a personal vendetta against my space bar.@@<>@@.you;$name: If I could program my computer to do anything, I'd make it play music for me while I'm working.@@ $classmateName: Honestly, I'd have it start a virtual coffee machine to keep me going during class. @@.you;$name: Ooh, I need that feature. I'd be so productive if my computer just gave me coffee on demand.@@<>@@.you;$name: I always get nervous when the computer asks me if I want to update. Like, what if the update ruins everything?@@ $classmateName: I swear, the only thing that updates faster than my computer is my panic when it asks. @@.you;$name: Exactly, it's like, “You want me to do *what* now?”@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you think computers ever get bored? Like, do they get tired of doing the same thing over and over?@@ $classmateName: Probably, but I bet they're just too polite to complain. @@.you;$name: Yeah, they're like, “Sure, I'll open 12 tabs and still function just fine.”@@<>@@.you;$name: I have a theory: Every time my computer freezes, it's because it's secretly thinking, “I need a break.”@@ $classmateName: I'm convinced my computer needs a vacation after I've had it running for too long. @@.you;$name: Maybe I should start giving it a little “me time.” Just turn it off for an hour.@@<>@@.you;$name: If computers could talk, I bet they'd complain about us clicking the wrong button all the time.@@ $classmateName: Definitely. They're probably like, “I told you not to click that!” @@.you;$name: It's like they know our next mistake before we even do.@@<>@@.you;$name: If my computer had a personality, it would be the grumpy old man who's always yelling at me to fix things I didn't break.@@ $classmateName: Mine would be the sarcastic friend who always tells me I'm doing it wrong, but in the nicest way possible. @@.you;$name: Exactly! It's like, “Sure, I'll fix that. Again.”@@<>@@.you;$name: Every time I restart my computer, I feel like it's resetting its entire life. Does it feel better afterward?@@ $classmateName: If it's anything like me, it probably just wants to go back to sleep. @@.you;$name: I get that. Restarting is like taking a nap for a computer.@@<>@@.you;$name: I wish I could control my computer with my mind. Like, just think about opening a program and boom, it's done.@@ $classmateName: Honestly, if that were possible, I'd just think “please work” and hope for the best. @@.you;$name: Same! It's like, “Can you please stop freezing now?”@@<>@@.you;$name: Why does every computer problem seem to require me to “just turn it off and on again”? I feel like that's the universal fix.@@ $classmateName: It's like the magic spell for technology. If in doubt, just reboot! @@.you;$name: It's a life hack at this point. Turn it off, take a deep breath, and turn it back on.@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you ever feel like computers are trying to take over our lives? They know everything about us.@@ $classmateName: They're like that friend who knows all your secrets but doesn't judge you for it. @@.you;$name: Yeah, and they store all of it in their memory for later use. No privacy in the digital world.@@<>@@.you;$name: I'm convinced my computer has its own schedule for when it decides to slow down. It's like it knows when I need it the most.@@ $classmateName: Yeah, it waits until I'm in the middle of something important to freeze. @@.you;$name: It's like a test of patience. Can you handle the chaos it causes?@@<>@@.you;$name: If I had a pound for every time I clicked the wrong thing, I'd be rich.@@ $classmateName: I'd be living in a mansion by now. Probably with a few extra hard drives to store all my mistakes. @@.you;$name: I'd buy a new computer and make it do all the work for me.@@<>@@.you;$name: You ever click a link and hope it's what you wanted, but deep down, you know it's probably a scam?@@ $classmateName: I call that “the hope click.” It's a dangerous game, but sometimes you have to take risks. @@.you;$name: It's like living life on the edge. “Is this a prize or a virus?”@@<>@@.you;$name: If computers could write a diary, do you think they'd be bored with us?@@ $classmateName: Definitely. Every entry would be like, “Today, I opened more tabs. Nothing interesting happened.” @@.you;$name: It'd probably end every entry with, “User didn't update me again.”@@<>@@.you;$name: Sometimes I wish I could just have a conversation with my computer. Like, “What do you want, computer? What do you need?”@@ $classmateName: Honestly, I bet it would say “Nothing, but you need to stop clicking all the wrong buttons.” @@.you;$name: I'd have to apologize for all the accidental restarts.@@<>@@.you;$name: If computers had emotions, I'm pretty sure mine would be passive-aggressive. Every time it freezes, it's like, “You didn't save, did you?”@@ $classmateName: Same! Mine always freezes just when I'm about to hit *save*. @@.you;$name: It's like a cruel joke. “You think you're prepared? Think again.”@@<>@@.you;$name: You know how we use "ctrl + alt + delete" to fix problems? What if that's actually the computer's way of saying, “I'm done with you”?@@ $classmateName: It's like a computer's way of throwing in the towel. @@.you;$name: Like, “Okay, you've pushed me too far this time.”@@<>@@.you;$name: Sometimes I feel like my computer is a genie. I make one wish and it gives me three problems to fix.@@ $classmateName: Oh yeah, it's always like, “Sure, I'll fix that. But now your printer is out of paper.” @@.you;$name: Classic computer trickery. “Be careful what you wish for.”@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like every time my computer crashes, it's a little part of me that dies inside.@@ $classmateName: Yep, it's like watching all your work vanish into the digital abyss. @@.you;$name: It's just a black hole of productivity.@@<>

passages.name: artClassmateConvo
passages.source_raw: <><>@@.you;$name: Do you ever wonder if art students are just professional doodlers?@@ $classmateName: Honestly, we're just scribbling our way to a degree. @@.you;$name: At least it's an abstract interpretation of procrastination.@@<>@@.you;$name: If I make a bunch of random lines and call it “abstract expressionism,” will anyone actually buy it?@@ $classmateName: As long as you don't call it “just a mess,” you're golden. @@.you;$name: I'll call it “chaotic balance of color and form.” That should work.@@<>@@.you;$name: Sometimes I wonder if art classes are just an excuse to play with paint all day.@@ $classmateName: Honestly, it's the best part of the job. Paint is life. @@.you;$name: It's like being a kid again, but with more expensive supplies.@@<>@@.you;$name: Is there a limit to how abstract art can get before it's just a blank canvas?@@ $classmateName: I mean, if it's a blank canvas, that's just "minimalism," right? @@.you;$name: Oh, so I've been accidentally creating masterpieces for years.@@<>@@.you;$name: I swear, if I get one more “unfinished sketch” label on my work, I'm going to lose it.@@ $classmateName: I mean, technically, it's not unfinished-it's just “evolving.” @@.you;$name: I like that. "Evolving" sounds way more sophisticated than “I ran out of time.”@@<>@@.you;$name: I think the hardest part of art is deciding when to stop and when to keep going.@@ $classmateName: Yeah, there's always that moment when you're like, “I've definitely ruined this.” @@.you;$name: And yet, you keep adding one more layer, just hoping for a miracle.@@<>@@.you;$name: You know what would make this art class even better? A never-ending supply of snacks.@@ $classmateName: Honestly, a good snack makes all the difference when you're in the zone. @@.you;$name: I'll trade some paintbrushes for chips right now.@@<>@@.you;$name: I've been trying to paint a landscape, but it keeps looking like a weird blob. Maybe that's my style?@@ $classmateName: That's called “post-impressionism,” my friend. You're ahead of the curve. @@.you;$name: I'm basically a revolutionary artist, just without the fame.@@<>@@.you;$name: You ever draw something and realize it's way cooler than you intended?@@ $classmateName: All the time! That's the magic of creating art-you surprise yourself. @@.you;$name: It's like a happy accident, but without Bob Ross.@@<>@@.you;$name: If I had a pound for every time someone asked, “What does this mean?” I'd have a gallery by now.@@ $classmateName: Yeah, and I'd probably just say, “It's open to interpretation.” @@.you;$name: That's the art student's universal answer!@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like my “artistic process” is just me staring at a blank canvas and wondering why I'm doing this to myself.@@ $classmateName: That's called “creative block,” my friend. Don't worry, it happens to the best of us. @@.you;$name: Great, I'm just waiting for the “spark” to hit me.@@<>@@.you;$name: If I paint a picture of a cat, and it looks terrible, does it make me a bad person?@@ $classmateName: Nah, it makes you a cat-loving artist. Imperfect art is still art. @@.you;$name: So, it's abstract art. I like that excuse.@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you ever look at your art and just think, “What in the world was I thinking?”@@ $classmateName: Every time I finish something, I'm like, “Who let me do this?” @@.you;$name: It's part of the process-trust the chaos.@@<>@@.you;$name: I bet the hardest part of being an art teacher is trying to make sense of what we hand in.@@ $classmateName: Yeah, I wouldn't want to be the one to grade all these masterpieces. @@.you;$name: But hey, at least it's better than grading papers, right?@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you ever try to copy a famous painting, and it ends up looking like something from a nightmare?@@ $classmateName: Absolutely. I tried to do a Van Gogh, and it ended up more “abstract horror.” @@.you;$name: I guess that's where the “expressionism” part comes in.@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like my art is just me fighting against my own brain, trying to make something beautiful.@@ $classmateName: Same! It's like I have a vision, but my hand just does its own thing. @@.you;$name: My brain is like, “Make it perfect!” and my hand is like, “Nah, we're good.”@@<>@@.you;$name: Sometimes I think art is just a fancy way of saying, “I have no idea what I'm doing, but let's make it look cool.”@@ $classmateName: That's the true spirit of creativity-embracing the unknown. @@.you;$name: Exactly! Who needs a plan when you have paint and some wild ideas?@@<>@@.you;$name: I've been working on this sculpture for hours, and it still looks like a blob of clay.@@ $classmateName: Sculpture's a process. Maybe it's an “emerging” blob. @@.you;$name: It's like watching art evolve in real-time.@@<>@@.you;$name: I think art classes should come with a “do not disturb” sign. Just let me be in my creative zone for a bit.@@ $classmateName: You need to add some snacks in that zone, too. Creativity and food go hand in hand. @@.you;$name: Agreed! A pizza break in between strokes of genius.@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like I need to take an art break, but I don't know what to do with my hands.@@ $classmateName: Just start doodling. It'll be therapeutic, trust me. @@.you;$name: Doodling is just art's way of saying, “I'll figure it out later.”@@<>

passages.name: englishClassmateConvo
passages.source_raw: <><>@@.you;$name: Do you think Shakespeare would've been a good Twitter user?@@ $classmateName: Definitely. He'd have dropped some real deep quotes. @@.you;$name: “To tweet or not to tweet, that is the question.”@@ $classmateName: I'd follow him just for the dramatic flair.<>@@.you;$name: If I wrote a paper on why pizza is the true meaning of life, would that get an A?@@ $classmateName: Honestly, it would get you at least a B for creativity. @@.you;$name: Maybe I'll throw in a Shakespeare quote and call it “a classic interpretation of modern philosophy.”@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like writing essays is just a long-winded way to say, “I have no idea what I'm talking about, but let's make it sound smart.”@@ $classmateName: That's exactly it. Just sprinkle some big words, and you're golden. @@.you;$name: “In conclusion, the existential nature of... pizza.”@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you ever get so lost in a book that you forget to blink?@@ $classmateName: Oh, all the time. My eyes end up feeling like sandpaper. @@.you;$name: That's when you know you're reading a good one.@@<>@@.you;$name: If I start my essay with, “According to the wise philosopher, SpongeBob SquarePants...” would that be a good idea?@@ $classmateName: I mean, it'd make a strong opening. You're making bold moves. @@.you;$name: Just wait until I get to “The art of jellyfishing and its relation to modern-day conflict.”@@<>@@.you;$name: What do you think the meaning of life is? In literary terms, of course.@@ $classmateName: Probably like a long-running metaphor for an unresolved plot arc. @@.you;$name: So, we're all just characters waiting for our next chapter. Got it.@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like poetry is just a fancy way of saying, “I don't know how to explain this, but here are some cool words.”@@ $classmateName: Well, it's about capturing emotions in ways that normal language can't. @@.you;$name: So, it's basically like creating an emoji but with more feelings and less yellow.@@<>@@.you;$name: I have a deep question for you: Would Romeo and Juliet have worked out if they just communicated better?@@ $classmateName: Honestly, I think they just needed a group text. @@.you;$name: Or, you know, maybe an open and honest conversation would've saved them.@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like I'm living in a metaphor right now. I just don't know what it means.@@ $classmateName: We're all living in a metaphor, my friend. You just have to find the symbolism. @@.you;$name: So, my life is probably a subplot, right? Just waiting for a big twist?@@<>@@.you;$name: What if I write an essay entirely about how much I dislike writing essays? Would that be too on the nose?@@ $classmateName: Maybe, but you'd get extra points for honesty. @@.you;$name: I'll call it “An Exploration of Frustration in the Modern Academic System.”@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you ever think about how ridiculous “The Great Gatsby” is? Like, no one should ever fall in love with a guy who throws parties to impress a girl.@@ $classmateName: Right? It's like, “Bro, she doesn't care about your pool. Get a grip.” @@.you;$name: Honestly, Gatsby was just a rich guy with commitment issues.@@<>@@.you;$name: If I just insert “This is a metaphor” in every paper, will people think I'm a genius?@@ $classmateName: If it's in the right context, sure. Just make sure it sounds like it's deep. @@.you;$name: Like, “The red curtains represent the bleeding heart of society.”@@<>@@.you;$name: I can't tell if my English teacher is just really smart or if she's just confusing us on purpose.@@ $classmateName: She's a master of mind games. We're all pawns in her literary chess match. @@.you;$name: I feel like every lesson is a plot twist.@@<>@@.you;$name: What if all the books we read in class are secretly trying to teach us how to live our lives?@@ $classmateName: Yeah, they're like hidden self-help guides disguised as literature. @@.you;$name: I guess *Moby Dick* was just a lesson in following your dreams, even if they're whales.@@<>@@.you;$name: If I wrote an essay on the life lessons from Harry Potter, would anyone take me seriously?@@ $classmateName: Absolutely. Harry Potter teaches us about friendship, bravery, and how to survive a magical world. @@.you;$name: I'll throw in a quote from Dumbledore for extra points.@@<>@@.you;$name: Can we just agree that Hamlet would've been way happier if he had a good therapist?@@ $classmateName: Absolutely. Imagine him just sitting down and unloading about his uncle. @@.you;$name: “So, tell me about your relationship with your father...”@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you ever feel like every character in a book is just an exaggerated version of ourselves?@@ $classmateName: Yeah, it's like we're all just walking metaphors for something deeper. @@.you;$name: I'm probably the side character who's just there for comic relief.@@<>@@.you;$name: I feel like every time I start writing a paper, I'm an artist trying to sculpt a perfect sentence. It never works out.@@ $classmateName: Welcome to the club. Every sentence is a masterpiece, until it's not. @@.you;$name: Then it's a “first draft,” and we don't talk about it again.@@<>@@.you;$name: I should start writing poetry, but I'm afraid my deepest thoughts are just about food.@@ $classmateName: That's still poetry! I'd totally read “Ode to Pizza.” @@.you;$name: It's a modern-day epic. “Cheese, oh cheese, you are my true love...”@@<>@@.you;$name: Do you think everyone reads books differently? Like, what if we're all just interpreting the same book in totally different ways?@@ $classmateName: Of course! Each person brings their own experiences and perspective to it. @@.you;$name: So, my version of *Pride and Prejudice* might be completely different from yours.@@<>

passages.name: mingleStudents
passages.source_raw: [img[img/schoolYard.webp]] You decide to mingle amongst the students. Many students walk amongst groups, predetermined who they will speak to for the entire school year. Teachers are sitting at a designated area. They're generally not interested in speaking to students. Some students are walking by themselves. Some are speaking on the phone, some are sitting under nearby trees, drawing or writing. Some are listening to music. The sun is wonderfully warm on your skin, almost too warm, but just good enough. You walk abit around for yourself, not sure where to go before you're approached by a student. <><><><><><> <><> That was funny. + Popularity | + Arousal [[Walk up to the teachers tables|mingleTeachers]] [[Return to class|school]] <><><><>

passages.name: theOACH
passages.source_raw: [img[img/schoolYard.webp]] You decide to join the overachievers. They look you up and down, then ask for your grade book. You'll need to have followed along in many classes before they'll consider you an over achiever as well. Popularity means nothing to them. The only thing they care about is school. And don't even think about skipping class! If any of these nerds find out you did, you'll be kicked off the team. This is not only about grades, but everyones collective future. If you ask them. The most they'll talk about is grades and earlier classes. If that's what you like, feel free to join them if you can, but you'll need to prove yourself first, that you're worthy of their time. You'll need skills in math, physics, english class, science and biology. Your math skills: $classSkill.mathematics Your physics skills: $classSkill.physics Your english skills: $classSkill.english Your science skills: $classSkill.science Your biology skills: $classSkill.biology <><>You've joined The Overachievers! You can now hang out with them during recess.<><><>You're not skilled enough to be considered an overachiever. Try again next time, bum!<> [[Leave|schoolSocialize]]

passages.name: theCREA
passages.source_raw:
[img[img/schoolYard.webp]]

You decide to join the creatives. They don't have any specific requirements for you to join them, only that you are kind and nice towards them, and contribute occassionally to conversations. They don't really care too much about their grades, as they believe true creative minds can't be graded properly. Of course, they care about school and their future, but being creative means more to them than following class if they can get away with it. They'll mostly talk about that, and not school.

You can join them if you like painting or art. Or really anything that is remotely creative.

<<linkreplace "Join The Creatives">>You've joined The Creatives! You can now hang out with them during recess.<<set $clique to $schoolCliques.creatives>><</linkreplace>>
[[Leave|schoolSocialize]]

passages.name: theATH
passages.source_raw: [img[img/schoolYard.webp]] You decide to join the over athletes. They look you up and down, judging how you look and present yourself. You'll need to be in good physical form to be allowed to join them. They're not the sharpest tools in the shed, but they sure are the strongest axe in the wood-chopper's van. They'll mostly do pushups and talk about muscle hypertrophy and anything else a jock likes to think about. You'll need to be able to take that to join these guys. You can join them if you have the nessecary body and skills to be able to compete with them. They like that. You'll need skills in cardio, strength and yoga. Your cardio skills: $cardio Your strength skills: $strength Your yoga skills: $yoga <><>You've joined The Athletes! You can now hang out with them during recess.<><><>You're not skilled enough to be considered an athlete. Try again next time, bum!<> [[Leave|schoolSocialize]]

passages.name: theGNT
passages.source_raw:
[img[img/schoolYard.webp]]

You decide to join the gamers and tech wizards. They don't have any specific requirements for you to join them, only that you are kind and nice towards them, and contribute occassionally to conversations. They look you up and down. It's not every day they see a girl this beautiful, and especially here. Girls don't want to talk to guys like these at the university, as they're typically more interested in the jocks. They'll likely be talking about Dungeons and also Dragons, if you're into those types of subjects. Maybe even Gathering the Magic.

You can join them if you like, though one of them is still eyeing you up and down. Mostly your body, not really your face. Mainly your boobs.

<<linkreplace "Join The Gamers & Tech Wizards">>You've joined The Gamers & Tech Wizards! You can now hang out with them during recess.<<set $clique to $schoolCliques.gamers>><</linkreplace>>
[[Leave|schoolSocialize]]

passages.name: theREB
passages.source_raw:
[img[img/schoolYard.webp]]

You decide to join the rebels. They don't have any specific requirements for you to join them, only that you are kind and nice towards them, and contribute occassionally to conversations. They look you up and down in their leather jackets. Some of them are pierced. Perhaps places you can't see as well? They smile at you, anticipating what you're coming to ask them.

Their "leader", Danny Sucko extends a hand in kindness. They've got a bad rep, but a pretty girl like you is always appreciated to join, he says. Besides, you're not who they're rebelling against.

<<linkreplace "Join The Rebels">>You've joined The Rebels! You can now hang out with them during recess.<<set $clique to $schoolCliques.rebels>><</linkreplace>>
[[Leave|schoolSocialize]]

passages.name: theSOC
passages.source_raw:
[img[img/schoolYard.webp]]

You decide to join the social butterflies. They look you up and down, then look between each others. You'll need high popularity to join them. The students in this clique care more about their image to others than their grades, and would do anything to not be "seen" as losers.

Your popularity: $popularity

<<if $popularity gte 40>><<linkreplace "Join The Social Butterflies">>You've joined The Social Butterflies! You can now hang out with them during recess.<<set $clique to $schoolCliques.socials>><</linkreplace>><<else>>You're not popular enough to be considered a social butterfly. Try again next time, bum!<</if>>
[[Leave|schoolSocialize]]

passages.name: theCHO
passages.source_raw:
[img[img/schoolYard.webp]]

You decide to join the chill outsiders. They don't have any specific requirements for you to join them, only that you are kind and nice towards them, and contribute occassionally to conversations. They don't do much, and don't engage much with the popular students, however in their own accord and their own little world amongst themselves, they're the popular ones. Who needs a thousand fake friends, when 3 or 4 real OGs can last a lifetime? At least, that's what these guys think. Some say, it's beceause they're weird, some say, they chose it themselves. To not interact with society changes a person.

<<linkreplace "Join The Chill Outsiders">>You've joined The Chill Outsiders! You can now hang out with them during recess.<<set $clique to $schoolCliques.chill>><</linkreplace>>
[[Leave|schoolSocialize]]
